reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports TiC dispersion and grain boundary strengthening in pure W, but it does not address W–Cu composites, Cu matrix effects, or the specific mechanisms of phase separation and void suppression at W–Cu interfaces. The key premise that TiC will stabilize W–Cu interfaces and improve thermal conductivity is therefore largely unsupported by the provided passage.
premises: TiC particles can be uniformly dispersed at grain boundaries and interfaces in W-based composites.
TiC at grain boundaries provides resistance to grain boundary migration at elevated temperatures.
TiC increases irradiation resistance in W-based materials.
TiC dispersion improves high-temperature mechanical stability (creep strength, hardness) in W-based composites.
These TiC benefits in W can be transferred to W–Cu composite interfaces to suppress phase separation and void formation.
